extracted.intended_audience: individual investors (retail investors) who wish to submit comments to the SEC
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for individual/retail investors on preparing and submitting public comments to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission during its rulemaking process, including what to say, how to say it, and how to submit it. Emphasizes tailoring comments to the rulemaking stage and avoiding disclosure of personal identifying information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept Release — provide preliminary feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Concept Release: The SEC seeks preliminary feedback by outlining topics and presenting potential approaches before formal proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When responding to a Concept Release, the bulletin implies you should offer early-stage input on topics and potential approaches rather than comment on final rule text. Focus on high-level concerns, alternatives, and reactions to the range of approaches described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposing Release — comment on proposed text and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposing Release: The SEC publishes a formal proposal containing the proposed rule text, its purpose, and economic analysis for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a Proposing Release, comment specifically on the proposed rule text, the stated purpose, and the supporting economic analysis. Identify precise language in the proposed text and discuss anticipated effects and costs/benefits grounded in reasoning or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopting Release — expect explanations of comment influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting Release: After reviewing comments, the SEC issues a final rule with explanations of how feedback influenced the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that the agency will explain how it considered comments when issuing the final rule. This underscores the value of clearly reasoned input that the SEC can point to when explaining its decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study the proposal and available summaries beforehand
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the proposal and available summaries beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the full proposal and any agency summaries so your comment is informed. Familiarity with the proposal helps you identify relevant sections and reference the agency's stated purposes and analyses rather than relying on hearsay or incomplete information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe your investor background and personal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe their investor background and how the rule affects them personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your role (e.g., individual retail investor, small-business investor, pension plan participant), relevant experience, and specifically how the proposed rule would affect your investments, costs, or behavior. Personal impact statements help the SEC understand practical consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly identify specific sections being discussed with supporting reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly identify specific sections being discussed with supporting reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing the proposal, point to exact sections, paragraphs, or proposed rule text and explain why you support or oppose them. Provide logical reasoning, cause-effect claims, and, where possible, cite data or examples that support your position. Avoid vague generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose alternatives to opposed provisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you oppose a provision, offer concrete alternative language or approaches that would address your concerns. Constructive suggestions are more useful to the agency than mere expressions of opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include factual evidence when available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support your assertions with data, citations, examples, or documented experiences. Evidence strengthens credibility and helps the SEC weigh the practical implications of comments against the agency's analytic record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SEC.gov online submission forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are submitted through online forms on SEC.gov's Rulemaking Activity page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments via the SEC's designated online forms to ensure they are received and included in the rulemaking record. Follow the submission instructions on the Rulemaking Activity page to ensure proper docketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid including personal identifying information (PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: The bulletin cautions that all comments become public, so investors should avoid personal identifying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because comments are posted publicly, do not include sensitive personal data (e.g., Social Security numbers, account numbers, home address) or other PII. Consider whether personal contact details are necessary; if not, omit them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of transparency and duplicate-submission handling
rubrics_metrics.description: "Comments received through this process are considered in the rulemaking" and subsequently posted publicly. Duplicate submissions result in only the first being published with a tally of repetitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know that submitted comments enter the public record and that duplicate submissions are tallied but only the first is published. Avoid filing unnecessary duplicates; if coordinating a submission, understand the SEC's public posting and counting practices.
